extracted.intended_audience: aspiring poets and literary critics (readers/writers of 18th-century poetic criticism)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing and judging poetry and poetic criticism, emphasizing diction, prosody, use of examples/allusion, and moral/stylely decorum. Includes rules for prosody (syllable variety, feet), tone matching, and critical manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Envy and Detraction
rubrics_metrics.description: There is nothing which more denotes a great Mind, than the Abhorrence of Envy and Detraction. This Passion reigns more among bad Poets, than among any other Set of Men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and critics should avoid depreciating fellow-writers out of jealousy; true greatness is shown by generosity in praise. Building fame by attacking contemporaries is an inferior strategy; celebrated writers increase one another's lustre by mutual esteem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candour and Ingenuity in reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: How much more noble is the Fame that is built on Candour and Ingenuity, according to those beautiful Lines of Sir John Denham...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for a reputation founded on honest judgment and cleverness of expression rather than on tearing others down or on affected novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elegance and Perspicuity of expression
rubrics_metrics.description: The Observations ... are explained with that Elegance and Perspicuity in which they are delivered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When making critical observations (or teaching precepts), present them clearly and gracefully so readers readily assent; clarity plus elegance strengthens otherwise familiar points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid positive dogmatick criticism without language/genius/imagination
rubrics_metrics.description: There is nothing in the World so tiresome as the Works of those Criticks who write in a positive Dogmatick Way, without either Language, Genius, or Imagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical advice should not be dry, prescriptive dogma; it must be enlivened by good language, inventive thought, or imagination. Emulate classical critics' manner (Horace, Longinus) rather than mechanical rule‑listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give known things an agreeable turn (stylistic reinvention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit and fine Writing doth not consist so much in advancing Things that are new, as in giving Things that are known an agreeable Turn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since most ideas have been touched before, focus on presenting common truths in more beautiful, striking, or uncommon lights—shape and application of ideas matter more than pure novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemplify precepts with immediate instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Our English Author has after the same manner exemplified several of his Precepts in the very Precepts themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When stating a rule or precept, illustrate it by an example embedded in the rule itself; showing the rule in practice strengthens persuasive power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrain pathos; reserve tears for serious occasions
rubrics_metrics.description: these eloquent Drops may no more be lavished on Trifles, or employed as Servants to their wayward Wills; but reserved for serious Occasions in Life, to adorn generous Pity, true Penitence, or real Sorrow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid lavishing strong emotional effects on trivial subjects; deploy pathos only for genuinely serious occasions to retain force and avoid bathos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid insipid smoothness: vary syllable lengths and avoid expletives
rubrics_metrics.description: These Equal Syllables alone require, Tho oft the Ear the open Vowels tire, While Expletives their feeble Aid do join, And ten low Words oft creep in one dull Line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent monotonous 'equal syllable' lines that tire the ear: vary word lengths and avoid weak expletive constructions ('do', unnecessary auxiliaries) and long strings of short words that produce dullness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid needless Alexandrines and dragging lines
rubrics_metrics.description: A needless Alexandrine ends the Song, That like a wounded Snake, drags its slow Length along.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not tack on an unnecessary alexandrine (an extra-long line) that slows the poem's momentum; keep line-length appropriate to sustain pace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match sound to sense (prosody echoing meaning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tis not enough no Harshness gives Offence, The Sound must seem an Eccho to the Sense. Soft is the Strain when Zephyr gently blows... But when loud Surges lash the sounding Shore, The hoarse rough Verse shou'd like the Torrent roar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the musical qualities of verse—tone, diction, rhythm—reflect the subject matter. Use softer, smoother sounds for gentle scenes; rougher, heavier sounds and rhythms for violent or forceful action so that sound echoes sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use metrical feet to depict motion and weight
rubrics_metrics.description: It is admirably described in the Numbers of these Verses; As in the four first it is heaved up by several Spondees intermixed with proper Breathing places, and at last trundles down in a continual Line of Dactyls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select metrical feet deliberately—spondees and pauses can convey heaviness/labor, while dactyls or quicker feet can convey rolling or swift motion. Prosodic patterning should imitate the action described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodical regularity in prose criticism when required
rubrics_metrics.description: The Observations follow one another ... without that methodical Regularity which would have been requisite in a Prose Author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing prose criticism, maintain a clear, methodical organization appropriate to prose; poetic freedom of arrangement does not excuse unclear or disordered prose exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use apt allusions and place common precepts in beautiful light
rubrics_metrics.description: They are placed in so beautiful a Light, and illustrated with such apt Allusions, that they have in them all the Graces of Novelty...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enhance familiar precepts with well-chosen allusions and illustrative detail so they feel fresh and persuasive; apt allusions can make received wisdom appear novel.
